mates.name: Back-rank mate
mates.why: Black's own pawns box the king in. A rook or queen on the back rank finishes it. In your games: always give your king a flight square (h3 or h6) once the back rank gets dangerous.

mates.name: Smothered mate
mates.why: Knight checks, double check, then the queen sacrifice on g8 forces the rook to block the king's last square. The knight mates a king trapped by its own pieces.

mates.name: Anastasia's mate
mates.why: The knight on e7 covers g8 and g6. The rook swings to the h-file and the king has nowhere to go.

mates.name: Arabian mate
mates.why: Rook and knight together: the knight guards the rook and covers g8, the rook checks from h7.

mates.name: Boden's mate
mates.why: Two bishops on crossing diagonals mate a king castled long. One covers b8 and c7, the other checks from a6.

mates.name: Damiano's mate
mates.why: A pawn on g6 supports the queen on h7. Watch for this whenever a pawn reaches the sixth rank next to the king.

mates.name: Epaulette mate
mates.why: The king's own rooks sit on its shoulders like epaulettes, so a queen check from e6 is mate: d7, e7 and f7 are all covered.

mates.name: Opera mate
mates.why: Morphy's finish: the rook mates on d8 while the bishop guards it and covers e7.

mates.name: Légal's trap
mates.why: Black pinned your knight with ...Bg4, but the pin is fake: Nxe5! and if ...Bxd1, Bxf7+ and Nd5 is mate. If Black doesn't take the queen, you're simply a pawn up.
mates.line: 5. Nxe5 dxe5 6. Qxg4 Nc6 7. Qf3 Qd7 8. Ne2

endings.name: Win the pawn ending
endings.why: Only one move wins. Think opposition and key squares: your king belongs in front of the pawn, two squares ahead if you can, and you want the opponent to be the one who has to move away.

endings.name: Outrun the king
endings.why: Their king is far away, so count the race: if it can't reach the square of your pawn, just push. If it can, bring your king in front of the pawn first.

endings.name: Hold the draw
endings.why: Only one move draws. Head for the square in front of the pawn, and take the opposition when the kings face each other: the side that must move away loses ground.

endings.name: Catch the pawn
endings.why: Their king is far away, so it's a race. Picture the square from the pawn to its promotion rank: if your king can step inside it, you catch the pawn. Head straight for the square in front of it.

endings.name: Lucena: build a bridge
endings.why: The Lucena position is the most important winning rook ending. Your rook already cuts their king off. Lift it to the 4th rank (Rd4). When the side checks come, your king walks out toward the rook and the rook blocks the last check: that's the bridge.

endings.name: Philidor: hold the draw
endings.why: The Philidor defence: keep your rook on your 3rd rank (here the 6th) so their king can't come forward. The moment the pawn steps onto that rank, swing the rook behind the king and check from far away: the king has nowhere to hide.
